anomalies.observed: On both CAN transceivers, GND1 and GND2 are each connected to GND, so the two sides of each isolator share a ground net.
anomalies.expected: The CAN-side and logic-side grounds should remain separate for the stated isolated CAN interfaces; the CAN-side supply should also be isolated from the logic supply.

evidence.quote: U11 pins 4 GND1 and 5 GND2; both are connected to GND. U10 pins 4 GND1 and 5 GND2; both are connected to GND. (Sheet: /, page 1)
two isolated CAN buses ... through an isolated CAN transceiver (Sheet: cm4_robot_board, page 1)

anomalies.impact: The shared ground bypasses the transceivers' galvanic isolation, so the CAN interfaces cannot provide the intended isolation from the logic circuitry and may conduct ground differences or transients into it.

parsed.summary: The schematic ties both ground pins of each isolated CAN transceiver to the same GND net. This defeats the galvanic isolation specified for the CAN interfaces.
